name: Choose the next improvement
decision: what can I change to improve my solution?
description: Choose the next intervention from observed failures, evidence gaps, and performance bottlenecks; revisit other branches after evaluating it.

children.name: Repair incorrect execution
children.decision: Which failure should be repaired before interpreting model scores?
children.description: Choose the observed failure mode rather than treating broken inference as evidence about model quality.

children.name: Repair model compatibility
children.decision: Which model contract is inconsistent with the saved training configuration?
children.description: Choose the contract repair indicated by artifact, preprocessing, or alignment evidence.

children.name: Match architecture and weights
children.description: Reconstruct the saved model and tokenizer exactly and inspect strict checkpoint loading to repair missing, incompatible, or unintentionally initialized parameters.

children.name: Restore training preprocessing
children.description: Reproduce the checkpoint’s training-time tokenization, normalization, resolution, feature extraction, and available input fields at inference.

children.name: Align rows and feature columns
children.description: Join predictions and features by stable sample keys and restore the exact training feature order before combining arrays.

children.name: Repair a stage handoff
children.description: Trace named inputs, shapes, feature schemas, and configuration flags across pipeline boundaries to repair the first inconsistent handoff.

children.name: Repair prediction computation
children.decision: Which computation defect explains the implausible output?
children.description: Select the smallest arithmetic or control-flow repair supported by traced predictions.

children.name: Repair blending arithmetic
children.description: Check numeric array types, component variables, weight sums, and averaging denominators against an explicitly computed small example.

children.name: Repair output or objective mathematics
children.description: Compare output shapes, activations, loss derivatives, and reduction axes with the intended mathematical definition on a small batch.

children.name: Restore all intended predictions
children.description: Assert that each enabled fold or model contributes once and that the submission uses the final combined prediction array.

children.name: Trace constant predictions
children.description: Inspect real sample predictions through each stage to locate the wrong dataset, placeholder array, or inactive code path producing constant outputs.

children.name: Align prediction direction
children.description: Check each model’s score direction against held-out targets and invert outputs that represent the opposite ordering before blending.

children.name: Repair failed execution
children.decision: What prevents the intended inference run from producing a valid artifact?
children.description: Choose a dependency, device, interface, output, or missing-component repair from the observed failure.

children.name: Repair imports and artifact paths
children.description: Verify mounted files and package versions and repair the earliest missing import, invalid path, or incompatible dependency.

children.name: Use a supported device path
children.description: Place model and inputs on the same supported device and verify a CPU baseline before enabling hardware-specific execution.

children.name: Verify the submitted artifact
children.description: Check the required output path, schema, checkpoint availability, and production flags so the written file contains the complete intended predictions.

children.name: Repair the first failing operation
children.description: Run a minimal end-to-end example and fix the earliest reproducible API, variable, configuration, or data-loading failure before expanding the run.

children.name: Replace invalid fallback predictions
children.description: Use only verified, aligned cached predictions for failed components or exclude the failed component and renormalize the surviving blend.

children.name: Improve the evidence for a change
children.decision: What is missing before the next performance comparison can be trusted?
children.description: Choose a scored baseline, valid evaluation, representative split, or more informative experiment.

children.name: Establish a scored baseline
children.description: Run the smallest complete prediction pipeline and record its metric as the reference for subsequent experiments.

children.name: Repair evaluation validity
children.decision: Which source of misleading validation needs correction?
children.description: Choose between leakage removal, out-of-fold reconstruction, and validation-distribution diagnosis.

children.name: Remove label leakage
children.description: Exclude labels, identifiers used as targets, and in-sample predictions from feature or target-estimation paths before judging model quality.

children.name: Align out-of-fold predictions
children.description: Generate every stacking feature with shared fold indices and ensure each row was excluded from the base learner that predicted it.

children.name: Check validation credibility
children.description: Compare local validation rankings with earlier external scores and favor representative local evidence over tiny leaderboard differences.

children.name: Change the validation design
children.decision: Which split construction best represents the required generalization?
children.description: Choose the split boundary or fold structure from observed dependence and distribution evidence.

children.name: Preserve target proportions
children.description: Use target-stratified folds, binning continuous targets when needed, and verify the target distribution within each held-out fold.

children.name: Hold related examples together
children.description: Compare group-aware split variants that keep related examples together and match the task’s required generalization boundary.

children.name: Derive provisional groups
children.description: Cluster target-free representations to construct provisional validation groups when no meaningful group metadata exists.

children.name: Tune the validation fold count
children.description: Compare a small set of fold counts or nested versus flat splits while tracking held-out sample sizes and metric stability.

children.name: Probe subgroup-enriched folds
children.description: Test subgroup-enriched fold construction against a genuinely disjoint holdout, since overlapping train and validation rows in the source trajectories invalidate their local score as generalization evidence.

children.name: Choose the next comparison
children.decision: Which experiment will resolve the current uncertainty most directly?
children.description: Choose a controlled ablation, rollback, repeatability check, equivalence check, coordinated probe, or stopping decision.

children.name: Isolate one change
children.description: Toggle one changed component against a frozen baseline to attribute the observed score difference.

children.name: Restore a known good configuration
children.description: Restore the complete last verified configuration after a regression before testing further improvements.

children.name: Measure repeatability
children.description: Repeat identical inference with pinned artifacts and compare prediction arrays and score distributions to estimate execution variability.

children.name: Verify numerical equivalence
children.description: Compare predictions before and after a refactor on identical inputs and checkpoints before accepting the rewritten pipeline.

children.name: Probe a coordinated package
children.description: Test a small package of coupled changes against a saved baseline when establishing a useful operating region matters more than attributing each contribution.

children.name: End an exhausted sweep
children.description: Stop the current parameter sweep when its recent gains are no larger than observed variability and redirect the next experiment to another lever.

children.name: Change training evidence
children.decision: Which change to supervision should be tested next?
children.description: Choose a change to row usage, additional examples, or target construction.

children.name: Change how labeled rows are used
children.decision: Which change to the existing labeled population is justified?
children.description: Choose filtering, deduplication, resampling, weighting, or a final refit from the observed data problem.

children.name: Filter suspected label errors
children.description: Use out-of-fold residuals or label-quality evidence to remove a narrowly defined set of suspected outliers and compare against the unfiltered baseline.

children.name: Select a representative training subset
children.description: Compare inclusion and exclusion of identifiable low-quality or distribution-shifted training subsets while keeping evaluation fixed.

children.name: Deduplicate overlapping observations
children.description: Aggregate labels and remove repeated or overlapping observations before balancing the training sample population.

children.name: Resample underrepresented examples
children.description: Test subgroup resampling or within-class interpolation inside training folds and retain it only when disjoint validation improves.

children.name: Weight training examples
children.description: Use explicit sample weights for a distribution-relevant subgroup rather than classifier-specific parameters that do not apply to the fitted objective.

children.name: Refit with more labeled rows
children.description: After selecting the configuration, replace a development-only holdout restriction with full-data refitting or complete cross-validation training.

children.name: Add training supervision
children.decision: Which additional source of supervision can be tested?
children.description: Choose quality-controlled labeled examples or pseudo-labels based on available data and teacher quality.

children.name: Add filtered labeled data
children.description: Train with quality-filtered auxiliary labeled examples, optionally in a separate preliminary stage, and compare on the original task’s holdout.

children.name: Use pseudo-labeled examples
children.description: Train or evaluate a pseudo-labeled variant on additional unlabeled examples and retain it only if independent validation supports its contribution.

children.name: Change the training target
children.decision: Which target representation fits the outcome and scoring rule?
children.description: Choose pooled survival transforms, groupwise transforms, or reversible regression centering.

children.name: Transform censored outcomes
children.description: Fit and compare survival-probability, hazard, rank, or scaled targets that represent censored outcomes for the downstream learner.

children.name: Estimate targets within groups
children.description: Fit the survival-target transformation separately within metric-relevant groups and compare with a shared transformation using leakage-free folds.

children.name: Center the regression target
children.description: Compare training-fold target centering with a shared offset and invert the selected transformation consistently at inference.

children.name: Change the input representation
children.decision: Which representation change should be tested next?
children.description: Choose an encoding, text context, feature source, signal front end, or input extent modification.

children.name: Change basic feature encoding
children.decision: Which basic encoding change addresses the observed input problem?
children.description: Choose missing-value treatment, categorical mapping, or numeric normalization.

children.name: Choose model-aware imputation
children.description: Apply explicit imputation and finite-value checks to learners that cannot accept missing values while preserving appropriate native handling elsewhere.

children.name: Reuse fitted categorical mappings
children.description: Fit categorical encoders on training rows and reuse their mappings with an explicit unknown-category policy at inference.

children.name: Match input normalization to the learner
children.description: Compare domain or per-sample normalization with the existing scaler and use the selected transform consistently in training and inference.

children.name: Change what the text encoder sees
children.decision: Which text-input modification is warranted by the observed examples?
children.description: Choose content cleaning, tokenizer behavior, truncation length, or input context.

children.name: Test text cleaning against raw text
children.description: Ablate normalization, spelling correction, or entity-aware cleaning against the pretrained tokenizer’s raw-text baseline.

children.name: Use compatible tokenization
children.description: Use library tokenization options and training-compatible special tokens instead of inconsistent manual padding or vocabulary edits.

children.name: Adjust sequence truncation
children.description: Compare token limits that preserve observed truncated content while keeping the checkpoint and remaining inference settings fixed.

children.name: Change the encoded text context
children.description: Test paired inputs, separate text streams, or metadata prompts with checkpoints trained for that input format.

children.name: Change the feature source
children.decision: Which feature representation should replace or extend the current one?
children.description: Choose a sparse representation, semantic embedding, engineered group, metadata branch, or compact subset.

children.name: Tune sparse or topic representations
children.description: Compare n-gram coverage, document-frequency filters, or topic dimensions while holding downstream evaluation fixed.

children.name: Add fixed semantic embeddings
children.description: Append cached pretrained embeddings to the existing feature matrix and measure their marginal contribution after refreshing feature selection.

children.name: Test an engineered feature group
children.description: Add or ablate one interpretable interaction, linguistic statistic, or structural feature group against the current representation.

children.name: Add structured metadata features
children.description: Compare a metadata feature branch with the representation alone using fields that are available and consistently encoded at test time.

children.name: Select a compact feature set
children.description: Recompute fold-based feature importance or group ablations after feature changes and compare retained subsets rather than reuse a stale selection.

children.name: Choose a signal front end
children.decision: Which signal transformation is most justified for the next experiment?
children.description: Choose spectral extraction, artifact filtering, outlier clipping, channel derivation, rendering, or a direct image layout.

children.name: Tune the time-frequency representation
children.description: Compare spectral transform, window, hop, or sampling settings with matched training and inference preprocessing.

children.name: Change signal filtering
children.description: Test a justified notch, passband, filter order, or filtering backend with matched training and inference preprocessing.

children.name: Clip signal outliers
children.description: Compare a tighter raw-signal clipping range against the current range before spectral feature extraction.

children.name: Change derived input channels
children.description: Add or ablate a defined group of signal channels and use a model trained for the resulting channel layout.

children.name: Change spectral image rendering
children.description: Compare grayscale or alternate spectral color mappings while holding the represented signal and model training protocol fixed.

children.name: Change the signal-to-image layout
children.description: Compare spatial factorizations of the same multichannel sequence and train compatible image models for each layout.

children.name: Change retained input extent
children.decision: Which part of the input extent should be varied?
children.description: Choose spatial resolution, crop boundaries, or temporal context according to what information is being lost.

children.name: Tune input resolution
children.description: Sweep resolutions around the checkpoint’s training size with all other settings fixed and retain the supported accuracy and runtime tradeoff.

children.name: Tune the spatial crop
children.description: Perturb one spatial crop boundary at a time and compare matched models or validated inference variants.

children.name: Match the temporal context
children.description: Compare temporal windows aligned with the label’s scope to determine whether neighboring context helps or dilutes the target signal.

children.name: Improve an individual model
children.decision: Which modification to one learner should be tested next?
children.description: Choose alternative weights, a different predictor, a revised head, or a training change.

children.name: Reuse trained weights differently
children.decision: Which saved-weight choice is justified by the available artifacts?
children.description: Choose a different training run, stopping snapshot, or compatible weight average.

children.name: Select a trained run
children.description: Evaluate alternative compatible training-run checkpoints with fixed inference settings and keep the reliably best variant.

children.name: Select the stopping snapshot
children.description: Compare final-epoch, best-validation, and quality-subset-selected snapshots under the same inference pipeline.

children.name: Average compatible weights
children.description: Average compatible snapshots from one model’s training trajectory and evaluate the resulting weights against the original checkpoint.

children.name: Choose a different predictor
children.decision: Which alternative predictor addresses the current model’s limitation?
children.description: Choose a new algorithm, pretraining source, capacity, frozen-embedding learner, or retrieval-based predictor.

children.name: Change the learner family
children.description: Replace the current learner with a structurally different algorithm or backend on controlled inputs and compare its validated standalone performance.

children.name: Change the pretrained backbone
children.description: Compare compatible checkpoints from different pretraining families or domains while controlling preprocessing and evaluation.

children.name: Change model capacity
children.description: Compare smaller and larger versions with appropriately trained weights and matched evaluation rather than assuming more parameters improve performance.

children.name: Fit a shallow model on embeddings
children.description: Train a cross-validated linear or kernel learner on frozen pretrained embeddings as an alternative to end-to-end fine-tuning.

children.name: Use neighbors as predictive evidence
children.description: Retrieve similar training examples with an embedding model and test their labels or similarities as held-out predictive features.

children.name: Change how representations become predictions
children.decision: Which head or fusion modification should be compared?
children.description: Choose head capacity, pooling, active modalities, or the rule for combining branch embeddings.

children.name: Change the prediction head
children.description: Compare a shared, grouped, or attention-augmented prediction head while retraining compatible weights and holding the backbone fixed.

children.name: Change feature pooling
children.description: Compare pooling or representation normalization before the output layer using checkpoints trained for each tested head.

children.name: Change active input branches
children.description: Add or ablate one modality branch in a jointly trained model to measure its contribution against the existing branch set.

children.name: Change branch fusion
children.description: Compare concatenation with element-wise averaging of branch features using a classifier trained for the resulting dimension.

children.name: Improve how one model is fitted
children.decision: Which training intervention should be tested next?
children.description: Choose optimization, objective, regularization, tree complexity, or training-loop repair.

children.name: Change the optimization trajectory
children.decision: Which optimization setting is the next justified change?
children.description: Choose learning rate, decay schedule, optimizer, duration, or stopping rule from the training logs.

children.name: Tune the learning rate
children.description: Bracket the learning rate using convergence logs and controlled trials, retreating from rates that destabilize training.

children.name: Change the learning-rate schedule
children.description: Compare the existing decay schedule with a staged alternative while holding other optimizer settings fixed.

children.name: Change the optimizer
children.description: Compare an alternative optimizer with the current one using controlled training runs and appropriate learning-rate settings.

children.name: Tune training duration
children.description: Compare nearby training durations against the held-out learning curve to correct undertraining or overfitting.

children.name: Monitor the intended validation metric
children.description: Configure early stopping to use the correct held-out dataset, metric direction, and saved best iteration, then compare with fixed-duration training.

children.name: Change the prediction objective
children.decision: Which objective better matches the target and evaluation rule?
children.description: Choose distributional, independent-output, pairwise, ordinal, custom, or auxiliary supervision.

children.name: Train against distributional error
children.description: Replace a mismatched surrogate with the differentiable probability-distribution metric or an aligned objective and validate its gradients and outputs.

children.name: Use independent output losses
children.description: Compare imbalance-aware or independent-output objectives with the current loss and ensure the activation matches the target semantics.

children.name: Train pairwise ordering
children.description: Test a pairwise ranking objective for a ranking metric and compare its held-out contribution with pointwise training.

children.name: Use an ordinal formulation
children.description: Compare regression with an ordered or categorical prediction head and decode outputs consistently with the label range.

children.name: Validate and tune a custom objective
children.description: Check custom derivatives and objective constants and compare a bounded set of configurations without using held-out labels to fit training parameters.

children.name: Add an auxiliary target head
children.description: Test a joint regression and auxiliary classification head against the main-task-only model using the same validation splits.

children.name: Choose a regularization intervention
children.decision: Which training regularizer fits the input and observed overfitting?
children.description: Choose head dropout, mild image transforms, spectral masks, or mixed examples.

children.name: Tune head regularization
children.description: Compare dropout or multisample dropout strengths in the trained prediction head against the current setting.

children.name: Use mild image augmentation
children.description: Compare modest brightness, contrast, or geometric training transforms that preserve the task’s visual semantics.

children.name: Mask temporal or spectral regions
children.description: Apply training-only contiguous time-frequency masking and compare its regularization benefit against unmasked training.

children.name: Mix training examples
children.description: Compare ordinary and multi-example mixup while mixing labels consistently and checking the validity of the resulting inputs.

children.name: Tune tree complexity and regularization
children.description: Search a bounded neighborhood of tree depth, leaves, rounds, and penalties while controlling seeds and using reliable validation.

children.name: Repair training discipline
children.description: Retrain a weak component with explicit fold handling, batch loading, checkpoint persistence, and a validated training recipe.

children.name: Change how models are combined
children.decision: Which ensemble intervention should be tested next?
children.description: Choose membership, combination rule, score transformation, meta-features, or search effort.

children.name: Change ensemble membership
children.decision: Which membership experiment is most informative now?
children.description: Choose simplification, marginal member selection, new diversity, or repeated-run averaging.

children.name: Compare the best member with the blend
children.description: Evaluate a strong single model or model family against the complete blend to decide whether ensemble complexity is justified.

children.name: Select ensemble members by ablation
children.description: Add, remove, or replace one candidate at fixed aggregation settings and keep membership changes supported by marginal validation gains.

children.name: Choose a source of ensemble diversity
children.decision: Which source of different prediction errors should be added?
children.description: Choose a new family, input view, prediction head, or target encoding rather than adding arbitrary correlated members.

children.name: Add a different model family
children.description: Introduce an independently trained learner with a different inductive bias and measure its marginal contribution to the existing blend.

children.name: Blend different input views
children.description: Add predictions from models trained on different modalities, feature representations, or independently implemented pipelines.

children.name: Blend different prediction heads
children.description: Train alternative heads on the same backbone and test whether their prediction errors complement the current ensemble.

children.name: Blend different target encodings
children.description: Train comparable models on distinct valid target transformations and evaluate whether their aligned predictions improve the blend.

children.name: Average repeated training variants
children.decision: Which repeated-training dimension should be averaged?
children.description: Choose fold or seed averaging according to the available checkpoints and measured instability.

children.name: Average fold checkpoints
children.description: Compare the available fold-checkpoint average with smaller subsets while checking each fold’s contribution and artifact compatibility.

children.name: Average independently trained seeds
children.description: Add independently trained seed or run checkpoints incrementally and stop when additional averaging has no reliable benefit.

children.name: Choose a prediction combiner
children.decision: Which combination rule should replace the current one?
children.description: Choose global averaging, grouped averaging, conditional weights, or a fitted meta-model.

children.name: Choose linear averaging weights
children.decision: Which coefficient rule is supported by current validation evidence?
children.description: Choose uniform, tuned nonnegative, or signed coefficients.

children.name: Use a uniform average
children.description: Use equally weighted predictions as the aggregation baseline when model-quality differences or optimized weights are not reliable.

children.name: Tune global blend weights
children.description: Optimize a small set of global blend coefficients on cached held-out predictions and recheck them after a component changes.

children.name: Allow subtractive coefficients
children.description: Compare unconstrained or signed blend coefficients with a nonnegative blend on disjoint validation to test whether subtracting correlated errors helps.

children.name: Balance model groups
children.description: Average within related model groups before combining group predictions to prevent groups with more checkpoints from dominating implicitly.

children.name: Use conditional blend weights
children.description: Compare class- or sample-dependent weights with a fixed global blend when validation supports stable conditional differences between members.

children.name: Fit a regularized stacker
children.description: Train a simple regularized meta-learner on aligned out-of-fold predictions and compare it with direct averaging before increasing meta-model complexity.

children.name: Choose the space for averaging
children.decision: Which transformation should be tested before combining model scores?
children.description: Choose rank, scale, power, or logit-space comparisons based on metric semantics and member distributions.

children.name: Compare rank and raw averaging
children.description: Compare rank-transformed and raw prediction averaging with identical members after upstream prediction distributions change.

children.name: Standardize prediction scales
children.description: Fit ordinary or robust prediction scaling on training-fold outputs and refit the blend before evaluating against unscaled predictions.

children.name: Reshape scores before averaging
children.description: Compare a bounded concave power transform of component predictions with ordinary averaging under a fixed membership set.

children.name: Choose logits or probabilities
children.description: Compare averaging logits before activation with averaging activated probabilities using the task’s held-out metric.

children.name: Change the stacker inputs
children.description: Add or remove one source of out-of-fold predictions, embeddings, or auxiliary features and refit the meta-learner on the new schema.

children.name: Bound blend-search effort
children.description: Compare a moderate search budget with one controlled expansion and retain extra trials only when independent evidence improves.

children.name: Change inference or final output mapping
children.decision: Which inference-only intervention fits the metric and observed errors?
children.description: Choose extra prediction views, discrete mapping, probability calibration, targeted correction, or removal of existing post-processing.

children.name: Choose inference averaging passes
children.decision: Which extra inference passes are justified?
children.description: Choose label-preserving transformed views or genuinely stochastic passes according to the input semantics and model mode.

children.name: Average valid transformed views
children.description: Compare deterministic test-time views with a single-pass baseline, preserving label semantics and retesting after checkpoint changes.

children.name: Choose deterministic or dropout inference
children.description: Check evaluation mode and compare genuinely stochastic repeated passes with deterministic inference rather than repeating identical forward passes.

children.name: Choose an ordinal mapping
children.decision: Which mapping from continuous scores to discrete labels is supported?
children.description: Choose global cutpoints, distribution matching, subgroup cutpoints, or explicit tie handling.

children.name: Tune ordinal cutpoints
children.description: Compare simple rounding with target-specific cutpoints fitted on out-of-fold predictions, retaining continuous outputs for degenerate columns when allowed.

children.name: Match discrete label frequencies
children.description: Compare quantile mapping to known training label levels with ordinary thresholding only when the expected test label distribution is supported.

children.name: Use subgroup-specific cutpoints
children.description: Compare global thresholds with separately fitted subgroup thresholds and revert to global calibration when subgroup estimates are unstable.

children.name: Test explicit tie handling
children.description: Compare the metric’s native tie treatment with a reproducible tie-handling variant without perturbing meaningful score differences.

children.name: Choose a probability calibration change
children.decision: Which probability adjustment is justified by the observed miscalibration?
children.description: Choose global temperature, class-specific multipliers, or required range normalization.

children.name: Rescale logits
children.description: Compare a global logit temperature against the original outputs and evaluate its effect on the final blend or calibration metric.

children.name: Reweight class probabilities
children.description: Fit class-wise probability multipliers on held-out evidence and renormalize, comparing against the unadjusted distribution.

children.name: Enforce required output ranges
children.description: Apply the required probability or range normalization once and verify that the final outputs satisfy the task’s scoring contract.

children.name: Choose a targeted score correction
children.decision: What independent evidence justifies correcting individual predictions?
children.description: Choose a systematic offset, auxiliary classifier signal, or precise metadata rule.

children.name: Correct a systematic output offset
children.description: Test a validation-estimated offset, reference-example subtraction, or inverse target scaling against the unchanged prediction baseline.

children.name: Apply an auxiliary-signal correction
children.description: Test a bounded offset or confidence-gated correction driven by an auxiliary classifier while holding the base predictions fixed.

children.name: Apply a precise metadata rule
children.description: Test a narrowly justified metadata-based correction on affected target columns and reject rules unsupported by held-out examples.

children.name: Ablate existing post-processing
children.description: Disable the current correction with model predictions fixed to measure whether it remains useful after upstream changes.

children.name: Remove an execution bottleneck
children.decision: Which execution change enables more reliable or complete experiments?
children.description: Choose reduced resource demand, less repeated work, or deterministic execution.

children.name: Reduce peak resource use
children.decision: Which resource reduction preserves the intended prediction pipeline?
children.description: Choose memory release, smaller batches, or reduced precision from measured allocation behavior.

children.name: Release stage-local memory
children.description: Release models and large intermediates after their last use and clear framework caches before starting the next expensive stage.

children.name: Fit the batch to memory
children.description: Reduce or bucket inference batches to fit measured memory limits and verify numerical equivalence before increasing throughput.

children.name: Compare reduced precision
children.description: Evaluate mixed or half precision against full precision on identical examples and retain the faster mode only within acceptable metric drift.

children.name: Reduce repeated work
children.decision: Which execution change removes the measured iteration bottleneck?
children.description: Choose cached intermediates, resumable training, modular controls, or a local implementation optimization.

children.name: Cache expensive intermediate results
children.description: Persist versioned features, embeddings, or raw predictions so downstream experiments can reuse identical intermediate results.

children.name: Resume completed training stages
children.description: Save fold or stage checkpoints and run only unfinished training work while explicitly restoring all stages needed for final inference.

children.name: Parameterize model execution
children.description: Expose model identities, artifact mappings, and development flags through a shared configuration instead of editing scattered code paths.

children.name: Accelerate the measured bottleneck
children.description: Optimize a profiled metric, feature operation, or padding-heavy inference loop while checking prediction equivalence and row order.

children.name: Pin stochastic execution
children.description: Fix seeds, worker behavior, transforms, search results, and artifact versions so comparisons use reproducible inputs and execution.

unassigned.reason: Notebook progress-bar display and registration only; no reusable prediction-quality or resource-control intervention is established.
